scope_line: Scope: the dify monorepo (api, web, dify-agent runtime, packages, CLI, docker configuration, CI). The separately released dify-sandbox and plugin-daemon services are assessed through their configuration here. Dify Cloud and the plugin marketplace catalogue are out of scope.

MAL-01.evidence: Entity kinds (apps, workflows, datasets, tools) are fixed models (api/models); new kinds need code, migration and release.
MAL-01.alt_note: Apps and datasets behave like runtime-defined entities, though of fixed kinds.

MAL-02.evidence: Knowledge-base documents carry user-defined typed metadata fields (DatasetMetadata, api/models/dataset.py); app input variables are typed with validation. No privacy tag; one entity family.

MAL-03.evidence: Relations and lifecycle states are coded per feature (draft and published workflows, document indexing states).

MAL-04.evidence: Every app gets the same generated service API shaped by its input variables (api/controllers/service_api), plus an OpenAPI surface (api/controllers/openapi, fastopenapi.py); no per-app code. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Apps are a single entity family, not arbitrary defined types.
MAL-04.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-05.evidence: Publishing a new workflow version changes the app's API inputs and outputs live (api/services/workflow_service.py version handling).

MAL-06.evidence: Generated OpenAPI documents (api/controllers/openapi, API_SCHEMA_GUIDE.md), typed SDKs (sdks/) and structured errors. No dry-run. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Coverage of the whole API by the generated spec was not verified.
MAL-06.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-07.evidence: Workflow canvases and each app's web-app settings (branding, opening statement, suggested questions) are data edited by builders; there is no page layout editor.

MAL-08.evidence: Chat, completion and workflow web apps render intake forms generically from each app's typed input variables; list and detail views are hand-built.
MAL-08.alt_note: Intake is fully generic and logs and annotations views are generic across apps.

MAL-09.evidence: Design-system themes (packages/dify-ui/src/themes) and 1,401 locale files, with AI translation in CI (.github/workflows/translate-i18n-claude.yml); no tenant theme editor or text overrides.
MAL-09.alt_note: The locale pipeline includes AI translation.

MAL-10.evidence: Workflows and chatflows compose triggers (schedule, webhook, plugin triggers in api/core/trigger), conditions, iteration, code, HTTP, tool and LLM nodes in the UI; debug preview and single-step runs; draft and published versions.
MAL-10.alt_note: Versioned, testable and partly AI-assisted (generate_workflow_instruction_suggestions), but not simulatable against history.

MAL-11.evidence: Inbound webhook and plugin triggers with per-node retry settings and run logs; Dify does not publish its own entity lifecycle events to subscribers.

MAL-12.evidence: Code nodes run in the separate dify-sandbox service with a worker timeout (SANDBOX_WORKER_TIMEOUT 15) and all network traffic forced through the SSRF proxy (SANDBOX_HTTP_PROXY, docker/.env.example:193-201, api/core/helper/ssrf_proxy.py); triggered by workflow events and requests.

GOV-01.evidence: Design system (packages/dify-ui) with accessibility lint rules (lint.config.ts) and an axe-based accessibility E2E workflow that runs on demand for a chosen page and WCAG level (.github/workflows/accessibility-e2e.yml:4-21).

GOV-02.evidence: Per-feature logs only: authentication audit entities (api/services/entities/auth_audit_entities.py), app and workflow run logs; no generic audit store.
GOV-02.alt_note: Run logs are generic across apps.

GOV-03.evidence: Account deletion service and scheduled message cleanup with retention settings (api/services/account_deletion_service.py, api/schedule/clean_messages.py); no data-subject export.

GOV-04.evidence: RBAC resource and agent-access services (api/services/rbac_resource_service.py), SSRF proxy and plugin signature enforcement (FORCE_VERIFYING_SIGNATURE, docker/.env.example:236); no security scanning in CI.

GOV-05.evidence: Workflows keep numbered published versions (workflow_version_number_service); apps export versioned DSL; other surfaces are unversioned. The higher reading of 3 was dropped under the inventory rule (a 3 needs every default surface at 3): Surfaces other than workflows and app DSL are unversioned.

GOV-06.evidence: Draft and publish with debug preview for apps and workflows; no review step or proposal object.

GOV-07.evidence: Every publish is a manual human action; the agent runtime's ask-human layer (dify-agent/src/dify_agent/layers/ask_human/layer.py) gates agent actions, not changes.

GOV-08.evidence: Imported DSL is checked against the current DSL version and flagged when older or newer (api/services/dsl_version.py, app_dsl_service.py); plugins declare manifests and versions against a stable plugin SDK contract. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If version warnings on import do not count as automated compatibility checks.
GOV-08.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

ARC-01.evidence: Knowledge bases get vector and keyword indexes configured per dataset (api/core/rag); application lists use SQL with Redis caching.

ARC-05.evidence: Multi-tenant workspaces with per-app and per-tenant rate limits (api/libs/helper.py) and plan quotas; no noisy-neighbour detection.

ARC-06.evidence: No load or performance suite and no documented limits found (searched for k6, locust, benchmark and load test).
ARC-06.alt_note: Vector-database test suites exercise one surface.

DEL-02.evidence: API, worker, web, sandbox, plugin daemon, SSRF proxy and agent runtime are separate containers with separate deploy workflows (9 Dockerfiles; .github/workflows/deploy-agent.yml, deploy-knowledge.yml).

DEL-03.evidence: import-linter layer contracts for the backend (api/.importlinter:1-20) plus ESLint configuration for the frontend. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Whether the import-linter contract runs as a required CI check was not verified.
DEL-03.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

DEL-05.evidence: Main CI on pull requests with no draft filter runs API tests, web tests, style, migration and bundle-size checks (.github/workflows/main-ci.yml, db-migration-test.yml, web-bundle-size.yml); accessibility runs only on demand and there is no security scan.

MAL-13.evidence: Plugins extend models, tools, agent strategies, endpoints, data sources and triggers; workflow templates and DSL are declarative; there are no plugin points for UI, theme or text.
MAL-13.alt_note: Breadth across server surfaces is large.

MAL-14.evidence: Plugins run in the separate plugin daemon, signatures are verified by default (FORCE_VERIFYING_SIGNATURE true) and outbound traffic goes through the SSRF proxy (docker/.env.example:222-236).

MAL-15.evidence: Plugin developers connect a local plugin to a running Dify instance for remote debugging through the daemon's install port (EXPOSE_PLUGIN_DAEMON_PORT, docker/.env.example:222), with logs; builders debug workflows step by step. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Remote debugging configuration was read from settings, not exercised.
MAL-15.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-19.evidence: Each app can be exposed as an MCP server with its input schema as the tool definition and a per-app server credential (api/controllers/mcp/mcp.py); Dify also consumes MCP tools. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: No capability map for the platform as a whole.
MAL-19.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

MAL-20.evidence: End users complete tasks conversationally in Dify apps grounded on knowledge bases with tool actions; builders get natural-language generators for prompts, code, structured output and workflow instructions (api/core/llm_generator/llm_generator.py:432-813). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Admin natural-language authoring covers parts of a workflow, not whole definitions.
MAL-20.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

GOV-09.evidence: App-scoped API keys, OAuth and device-flow login (api/libs/oauth_bearer.py, api/services/oauth_device_flow.py), rate limits and per-call logs; no idempotency keys or dry-run.

MAL-16.evidence: One model-provider interface maps many LLM vendors onto a canonical model API (api/core/model_manager.py, provider_manager.py); data-source plugins map external content into canonical documents and chunks.

MAL-17.evidence: Plugin SDK covers credential schemas and OAuth, triggers with subscriptions, data-source sync and install and upgrade lifecycle; admins install from the marketplace; signatures verify publishers.
MAL-17.alt_note: Signature verification is a form of certification.

MAL-18.evidence: Service API is path-versioned (/v1) and documented; no deprecation windows or conflict handling.

EXP-01.evidence: Kernel of tenants, accounts, apps, workflows, datasets, conversations and messages, tools and plugins, served over web, API, MCP and IM channels; no business-domain nouns.

EXP-02.evidence: Recommended apps and knowledge-pipeline templates ship domain solutions as app definitions, knowledge and tools on an unchanged kernel (api/constants/recommended_apps.json, pipeline_templates.json).

EXP-03.evidence: App DSL export and import is a versioned bundle of app configuration, workflow graph, model settings and tool references (api/services/app_dsl_service.py, dsl_version.py), plus snippet DSL (snippet_dsl_service.py).

LRN-01.evidence: Per-app statistics and workflow run logs update as runs happen (api/controllers/console/app/statistic.py, workflow_statistic.py); tracing to external LLM-ops tools (api/core/ops).

LRN-02.evidence: Message feedback (rating, content, source) is linked to messages and conversations (api/models/model.py:296-335) and triaged through logs and annotations; the link to the app configuration version was not verified.
LRN-02.alt_note: Messages record the app configuration they ran with.

LRN-04.evidence: App statistics combine usage and satisfaction for one app; no joined usage, support and delivery models.
LRN-04.alt_note: Satisfaction joins feedback and usage for each app.

LRN-06.evidence: Dashboards only; suggestions exist for conversation questions, not for software change.

DEL-04.evidence: AI generators for code, prompts, structured output and workflow instructions assist builders one step at a time (api/core/llm_generator).

LRN-09.evidence: Before-and-after comparison is possible by hand from statistics and traces; nothing binds a published version to a baseline and decision. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If manual comparison does not count as a mechanism.
LRN-09.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 1 on the evidence above.

DEL-06.evidence: /console/api/version and /console/api/ping (api/controllers/console/system.py:27-37) and a worker health check (api/celery_healthcheck.py); no configuration snapshot.

DEL-07.evidence: Docker Compose stack, seeded E2E runs (e2e/scripts/seed-runner.ts) and branch-triggered dev deploys (.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml); no per-change ephemeral environment.
DEL-07.alt_note: E2E runs create seeded, disposable instances per change.

DEL-08.evidence: Web and CLI E2E suites (.github/workflows/web-e2e.yml, cli-e2e.yml); no changed-path map or adoption instrumentation at ship.

LRN-07.evidence: Admins turn logged answers into annotations that the app reuses for similar questions (api/services/annotation_service.py); nothing proposes changes without being asked.

LRN-08.evidence: Annotations and app changes are applied by people without evaluation against a baseline.

ARC-02.evidence: Alembic migrations with downgrade steps (api/migrations/versions, 219 of 219); no enforced online strategy.

ARC-03.evidence: Stateless Flask API and Celery workers over PostgreSQL and Redis, documented through Docker Compose; no scale-out tests or manifests in the repository.

ARC-04.evidence: Celery queues with retries on many tasks (api/extensions/ext_celery.py, api/tasks/delete_conversation_task.py:104); no dead-lettering or idempotency rule.

ARC-07.evidence: Optional OpenTelemetry and Sentry; no metrics or objectives for core paths.

ARC-08.evidence: Model load balancing with cooldown across credentials (api/core/model_manager.py:68-130); plugins run in a separate daemon and code in a sandbox service. Connectors and internal services have no breakers, so a 3 is not defensible under the inventory rule.

ARC-09.evidence: No backup command; Docker volume backup is left to operators.

DEL-01.evidence: No request or feature-request object for changing the product was found; requests live outside it.

DEL-09.evidence: Published app versions go to all users at once.

DEL-10.evidence: Apps can switch their web app and API off at runtime (api/models/model.py:445-446).

LRN-03.evidence: End users like or dislike answers and the feedback is queryable per app (api/models/model.py:1299-1302); workflow runs record node errors.

LRN-05.evidence: Run traces show node-level errors per run; there is no grouping.

GOV-10.rationale: No self-change path: AI drafts are saved by a person.

EXP-04.evidence: No record of unmet intents was found.

EXP-06.evidence: Plugins from the marketplace are installed per workspace (api/services/plugin); no success metric or keep-or-kill record.

DEL-11.rationale: Scope fact code_release_path is false: No first-party evolution system ships code changes.

limits: Repository evidence only, main at the tip named above. dify-sandbox and plugin-daemon are separate repositories; their behaviour was taken from configuration here and not read in source. Dify Cloud and enterprise editions are out of scope. Single rater.
reading: **SAL 1.** Builders reshape apps and workflows without code (Open 2.2), and the AI generators draft prompts and code (DEL-04 2), but there is no intake (DEL-01 0) and no load suite (ARC-06 0), which caps the architecture foundation at L1. **Issue → Fix:** end users' likes and dislikes are recorded per app (LRN-03 2), but there is no grouping or diagnosis (LRN-05 1). **Next level:** structured requests, failure grouping, and measured capacity.

persistent_data.evidence: Apps, datasets and logs in PostgreSQL; vectors in a vector store; files in object storage.

multi_tenant.evidence: Workspaces (tenants) share a deployment with per-tenant limits.

hosted_service.evidence: API, Celery worker, web, sandbox and plugin daemon run as long-lived services.

machine_actions.evidence: The console and service APIs change apps, datasets and workflows.

agent_mutations.evidence: AI generators draft prompts, code and workflow steps into the editor; a person saves and publishes (api/core/llm_generator).

evolution_auto_apply.evidence: Every publish is a manual human action.

definition_change_path.evidence: Apps, workflows, prompts and datasets are definitions.

code_release_path.evidence: No first-party evolution system ships code changes.
